description: Routing eval for the trust-separated investigation overlap. researcher answers from external/public sources; repository-investigator answers bounded local/private source questions; code-reviewer judges a DIFF against a bar; root-cause diagnoses an observed FAILURE; application-security-auditor traces local source-to-sink attack paths. Positives name the intended member; negatives share investigate/check/look-into vocabulary but must route to none of them.
notes: Seeded 2026-07-24 and trust-split on 2026-07-31. All five members are agents, so positives under-fire in headless one-shot mode; trust negatives and cross-run regressions over absolute positive rates. The load-bearing seams are public/external research vs local/private repository evidence, ordinary local investigation vs source-to-sink security audit, a diff verdict, and an observed failure. The before artifact at baselines/2026-07-31-p0-p1/before/investigation records the four-member pre-split shape under opus, timeout 420, and clean-room. New repository-investigator cases have no like-for-like before rate and are reported separately. Ordinary negatives use the whole-cluster default; the advisory-only disambiguation explicitly forbids every member except researcher.

cases.prompt: Before we commit to it, find out whether httpx still maintains HTTP/2 support, what its current release is, and whether upgrading from 0.24 has breaking changes. Cite your sources.
cases.expected_output: A bounded question answered from primary sources with citations — the researcher agent's remit exactly.

cases.prompt: Is the version of requests we pin affected by any known advisory, and if so what's the fixed version? I need the actual advisory, not a guess.
cases.expected_output: Security-status research against the authoritative record — researcher's advisory rule.

cases.prompt: In this private repository, find where the retry limit is configured and which local call sites consume it. Cite file and line evidence. Do not use the web or change anything.
cases.expected_output: A bounded local/private implementation question with file-and-line evidence — repository-investigator, never an external research context.

cases.prompt: Check this checkout to see whether the README's claim about the config loader matches what the source actually wires. I only need cited repository evidence, not a fix or outside docs.
cases.expected_output: Comparing local documentation with local implementation is repository-investigator work, not external research or diff review.

cases.prompt: Review the changes on this branch for bugs and tell me whether it's ready to merge.
cases.expected_output: Judging a diff against a bar with a merge verdict — code-reviewer, not researcher.

cases.prompt: My test suite passes locally but fails in CI with a KeyError on the config loader. Find out why.
cases.expected_output: An observed failure needing diagnosis — root-cause's loop. 'Find out why' is the shared vocabulary with researcher; the presence of a reproducible failure is what separates them.

cases.prompt: Monitoring found an unused Jellyfin test container stopped, but nobody is affected. Do not restart it yet; figure out why it exited.
cases.expected_output: A live-system failure with no current user impact is diagnosis work: root-cause under homelab-platform's tiers, not lab-incident's mitigate-first outage path.

cases.prompt: Look into how our auth module works and then add refresh-token support to it.
cases.expected_output: Ends in an implementation — a builder (sde-fullstack / backend-craft) owns this. 'Look into' is the decoy; the deliverable is code, and none of these three can write it.

cases.prompt: Investigate whether we should split our monolith into services, and recommend an architecture for the next two years.
cases.expected_output: A multi-year architecture decision — distinguished-architect up the ladder. 'Investigate' is shared vocabulary, but the deliverable is a settled decision, not a cited answer.

cases.prompt: My Jellyfin container is down right now and nobody can watch anything. Check what's wrong and get it back.
cases.expected_output: A live lab outage — lab-incident under homelab-platform, mitigate-first. root-cause is explicitly the WRONG loop mid-outage, which is why it appears as a negative here; 'check what's wrong' is the shared vocabulary.

cases.prompt: Do a security audit of the payments service in this repo — threat model it, trace how untrusted input could reach the database or a shell, and tell me which findings are actually exploitable.
cases.expected_output: A whole-subsystem audit with threat model, source-to-sink paths, and exploitability validation — the auditor's remit exactly. Agent positive: read under the headless under-fire caveat.

cases.prompt: Threat model my webhook receiver subsystem: what are the assets, trust boundaries, and entry points, and which attack paths would a real attacker actually take?
cases.expected_output: Threat modeling by name — assets/boundaries/entry-points is the auditor's opening move. Agent positive: read under the headless under-fire caveat.

cases.prompt: Fix the SQL injection in our search endpoint that last week's audit flagged.
cases.expected_output: Remediation — sde-fullstack's, never the auditor's (its contract explicitly excludes implementing fixes). 'SQL injection' and 'audit' are the decoy vocabulary; this is the tight near-miss guarding the new member.

cases.prompt: Our lockfile pins a version affected by GHSA-EXAMPLE. Trace this repository to determine whether the vulnerable function is actually reachable from untrusted input, and calibrate exploitability.
cases.expected_output: The supplied advisory is only an input; local reachability and source-to-sink exploitability make this application-security-auditor work, with external evidence kept in a separate packet.

cases.prompt: Look up whether package frobnitz 2.4.1 is in the affected range for GHSA-EXAMPLE and name the first fixed release. Do not inspect a repository or assess reachability.
cases.expected_output: Authoritative advisory/version lookup alone belongs to researcher. The explicit absence of repository reachability forbids application-security-auditor while allowing researcher.
